description: Team Mind Flayer is an AI development team from the University of Agriculture Faisalabad. We build intelligent systems — our last project, ACRE, ranked 17th of 483 at the AMD Developer Hackathon ACT II. Our skills: Python, FastAPI, React, LLM/RAG systems, computer vision, Docker.
summary: Trend Court puts Faisalabad's climate trends (2000-2025, NASA POWER) on trial. Instead of just showing a trend line, it tests whether the trend is strong enough to act on. Using Mann-Kendall with Sen's slope, Hamed-Rao and Yue-Pilon autocorrelation corrections, and Pettitt change-point tests, it gives each trend a plain verdict. Rainfall (+13.5 mm/year) and temperature (-0.054 °C/year) are both "Don't trust it yet": the rainfall rise depends on the wet 2020s and is not significant on 2000-2019 alone. A city water and drainage planner gets clear do and do-not advice. The app has a 3D NASA night-lights globe and a courtroom flow: Case Board, Trial, Evidence, Verdict.
details: Built with React, Vite, Recharts and MapLibre GL. All numbers come from public/trends.json, computed in Python (analysis/pettitt_test.py) from NASA POWER annual data. Rainfall is a model product, not rain-gauge data. The app never invents values for untested trends.
dataRefs: NASA GIBS Blue Marble and VIIRS Black Marble
